input.question: Does there exist a metrizable topological group G that is o-bounded, meaning that for every sequence (U_n) of neighborhoods of the identity there is a sequence (F_n) of finite subsets of G such that G is contained in the union of the sets F_n U_n, and for which Player I nevertheless has a winning strategy in the game OF(G)? In this game, at each stage n, Player I chooses a neighborhood U_n of the identity and Player II chooses a finite subset F_n of G; Player II wins exactly when G is contained in the union of the sets F_n U_n.

rewritten_question: Does there exist a metrizable topological group G with the following two properties? First, G is o-bounded: for every sequence of neighborhoods (U_n) of the identity element, there are finite subsets F_n of G such that G is contained in the union of the left translates F_n U_n over all n. Second, in the open-finite game OF(G), where in inning n Player I chooses a neighborhood U_n of the identity and Player II chooses a finite subset F_n of G, with Player II winning exactly when G is contained in the union of F_n U_n over all n, Player I nevertheless has a winning strategy?

paper_evidence.quote: A subset A of a topological group G is called o-bounded if for any sequence (Un)n∈ω of neighborhoods of the origin of G there is a sequence (Fn)n∈ω of finite subsets of G such that A ⊂ ⋃ n∈ω FnUn.

Next, given a subset A of a topological group G, consider the following game OF(A) (abbreviated from Open-Finite). Two players, I and II, choose at every step k ∈ ω a neighborhood Un ⊂ G of the origin, and a finite subset Fn of G, respectively. At the end of the game, the player II is declared the winner if A ⊂ ⋃ n∈ω FnUn.
Problem 11 (Banakh). Is there a (metrizable) o-bounded topological group G such that the player I has a winning strategy in the game OF(G)?

Such a group, if exists, cannot be analytic and abelian (more generally, a SIN-group). On the other hand, the group Z^ω contains a dense o-bounded Gδ-subset A such that the first player has a winning strategy in the game OF(A), see [5].
Proposition 9. Let G be a topological group such that the underlying topological space is Menger. Then the first player has no winning strategy in the game OF on G.

Corollary 10. Let X be a non-σ-compact metrizable space such that all finite powers of X are Menger (Hurewicz). Then all finite powers of F(X), A(X), Lp(X), L(X), and Ls(X) are OF-undetermined being Menger (Hurewicz) groups which fail to be strictly o-bounded.
